newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says to launch mark Eurobond in early March.
newsitem.headline: Russia says to launch mark Eurobond in early March.

text.p: Russia will launch a one billion mark ($609.3 million) Eurobond to be led by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and CS First Boston in early March and will issue a total of about $3 billion in Eurobonds this year, Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Monday.
He also told Reuters that Russia's London Club debt rescheduling would close at the end of March or early April when the long process of reconciliation is completed.

Kasyanov said he expected the Eurobond to be priced similarly to Russia's first, about 350 basis points over U.S. Treasury bonds, and said Russia would issue a total of two or three Eurobonds this year.
Russia's debut post-communist Eurobond was in November and priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. It was heavily oversubscribed.
Kasyanov said the government had already approved the appointment of the lead-managers on Monday.
"The decision was made today. The size of the issue, as usual, we will announce shortly before the launch."
Kasyanov said the new mark Eurobond would be aimed at investors in European countries such as Germany, Austria, Switzerland and Benelux.
He said further issues this year could include another dollar-denominated Eurobond. He said Russia had not yet decided whether to issue in other currencies besides marks and dollars.
The first Russia Eurobond was $1 billion.
Separately, he said that Russia was negotiating with London Club banks.
He reiterated that after closing, Russia would pay the banks $2 billion in cash, distributed according to the amount of Russian debt held.
The $2 billion represented an advance payment of 25 percent of Russia's interest arrears, he said.
He said Russia would cover the remaining 75 percent of overdue interest by issuing 20-year notes in the name of Vneshekonombank, which would be listed in Luxembourg.
